Lucifer's Diary frontend codebase inventory. Repository root: /Users/taha/Claude projects/LucifersDiary. Frontend at frontend/. READ frontend/AGENTS.md FIRST.

Task: Inventory the tag filtering UI. The user wants Flip-plugin-style smooth reorder when tag filters toggle. Find: (a) TagBar component (used on browse + tag pages), (b) how filtering works — server-driven via URL params (likely, given Next.js App Router) or client-side state filter, (c) the cards / list that re-orders when a filter changes, (d) the search page (app/search/page.tsx), (e) anywhere else there is a filter-list pattern (BlockedTagsButton? TagPicker in admin?). Output: files, components, current behavior (is filtering server- or client-side? this is critical for whether Flip can be used directly), integration points, and a note in `notes` on whether server-side filtering blocks Flip (since Flip needs the same DOM elements before and after; a Server-Component re-render swaps the tree) and what the workaround would be.

input.area: Tag filtering UI — TagBar, browse/search/tag pages, BlockedTagsButton, admin TagPicker
components: TagBar (default export, components/TagBar.tsx) — single-line horizontal-scroll pill row, plus an expanded letter-grouped mode (A/B/C/…), with safe/adult color variants and a gold-stroke active state
CollapsedRow + Pill + Chevron (internal helpers inside TagBar.tsx)
CardGrid (components/CardGrid.tsx) — grid container the result cards live in, with a GSAP stagger-reveal on first scroll into view
StoryCard / SeriesCard / ChapterCard — the card items that re-render when a tag changes
BrowsePage (app/browse/page.tsx) — uses <TagBar basePath="/search"> as a discovery bar (no activeIds; clicking always navigates to /search?tagIds=…)
SearchPage (app/search/page.tsx) — async server component, reads searchParams.tagIds, refetches getStories/getSeriesList, renders <CardGrid> with StoryCard/SeriesCard

TagPage (app/tag/[slug]/page.tsx) — single-tag landing; resolves slug -> tag.id then renders the same CardGrid layout. Notably does NOT render a TagBar — selecting another tag means navigating back through /search

BlockedTagsButton (components/BlockedTagsButton.tsx) — header trigger panel for per-device tag blocklist; client-side, in-panel search filter + memoised sortedTags reorder (blocked rows pinned top, then alpha)
TagPicker (app/admin/_components/TagPicker.tsx) — author-form picker; selected pills pinned top, unselected pool sorted adult-first then alpha, filtered by a search input
input.currentBehavior: "Filtering is server-driven via URL params. TagBar is a 'use client' component but it only renders next/link <Link> elements — every pill href is built by buildTagHref(id), which writes ?search=…&tagIds=<id> against basePath (default /search), and the 'All' pill href clears tagIds. There is no client filter state and no router.push: clicking a tag is a Next.js App Router navigation. SearchPage and TagPage are async Server Components that read searchParams (or the route slug), call getStories / getSeriesList with the new tagIds, and render the next CardGrid tree. The result cards (StoryCard / SeriesCard inside <CardGrid>) are wholly re-rendered each navigation — they're brand-new DOM nodes with new React keys (story.id / series.id). CardGrid's only animation today is a one-shot GSAP scrollTrigger fade-up stagger that fires once on mount (`once: true`), so subsequent filter changes don't animate the cards at all. The only places filter toggles ARE client-side and could host Flip cheaply: (1) BlockedTagsButton — useMemo sortedTags reorders the in-panel <ul> when blocked toggles or filter text changes, all in the same component tree; (2) TagPicker in admin — useMemo {selected, results} similarly reorders pills when toggle() flips a value or query changes. TagBar's own active-pill restyle does not reorder pills (sortedTags is purely alphabetical, independent of activeSet)."
input.integrationPoints: "For the primary tag-filter reorder (browse/search/tag): every filter click triggers an App Router server navigation, so the cards being reordered come from different React renders / different DOM nodes. Hook points where a FLIP-style transition could be wired in: (1) TagBar.tsx — replace the next/link <Link> on each Pill with a router.push using useRouter + useSearchParams, then drive the reorder client-side OR keep <Link> and intercept onClick with e.preventDefault before the navigation to record First positions; pair with a useGSAP/useLayoutEffect on CardGrid keyed by serialised tagIds to read Last positions and tween the deltas. (2) CardGrid.tsx — already wraps the card list and has containerRef + useGSAP; this is the natural home for the FLIP read/play loop, and it would need stable card identity exposed (e.g., data-flip-id={story.id || series.id} on StoryCard / SeriesCard root) so the same id can be matched across renders. (3) The two server pages (app/search/page.tsx, app/tag/[slug]/page.tsx) currently pass children directly into <CardGrid>; no API contract change required as long as the cards expose a stable id attribute. (4) For BlockedTagsButton + admin TagPicker the reorder is fully client-side inside one component — Flip can be wired in directly around the useMemo sort with no routing involved. (5) SearchBar at components/SearchBar.tsx already does a router.push, confirming useRouter is the established pattern for query-string updates."
input.notes: "Yes — server-driven filtering is the central blocker for a vanilla GSAP Flip plugin integration on TagBar/browse/search/tag pages. Flip's contract is read-Before -> mutate-DOM -> read-After -> animate-delta on the SAME DOM nodes (or, with Flip.fit / data-flip-id, on nodes that survived a React reconcile in place). A Next.js App Router navigation re-renders the server tree, swaps the entire <CardGrid> subtree for a fresh React mount, and discards the previous DOM nodes before Flip could ever read 'After'. Three viable workarounds, ordered by intrusiveness: (1) Lightest — let Next.js fetch but intercept the render: in TagBar replace the <Link> with router.push + Flip.getState(cards) called synchronously BEFORE push, then in CardGrid run a useLayoutEffect keyed on the searchParams tagIds (or a serialised version) that calls Flip.from(savedState, …) after the new server render mounts. React preserves DOM nodes that share the same key across renders, so as long as StoryCard/SeriesCard expose data-flip-id={id} and the parent grid is the same DOM container, GSAP can match the surviving ids and animate their position deltas; cards that appeared/disappeared get Flip's onEnter/onLeave handlers. The 'savedState' has to live somewhere that survives the navigation — a module-level Map keyed by a session-scoped token, sessionStorage, or a React context that the new server render's first useLayoutEffect drains. (2) Move filtering client-side: convert SearchPage from a Server Component to a small server shell that fetches a superset of cards once and a client component that filters locally on tagIds in URL or local state. Flip then runs in a single component with all DOM intact. Drops SSR result counts and breaks the /tag/[slug] SEO landing pages — significant. (3) Hybrid: keep server filtering for deep links / SEO but optimistically perform the new filter client-side from a cached over-fetched dataset, then reconcile with the server payload on arrival. Most work, smoothest UX. For the two purely client-side filter surfaces — BlockedTagsButton's tag list and admin TagPicker — Flip drops in cleanly with no routing surgery: wrap the useMemo sort with Flip.getState before the state change and Flip.from after, keyed on tag.id. Those are good prototypes before committing to option (1) for the main browse path. Also worth noting: CardGrid's current GSAP stagger uses `once: true`, so it would need to be guarded to not fight a Flip tween on re-render."
